svg.title: FieldLink status sync: from one conversation per line to read, plan, write
svg.desc: Top band: version 0.1 handles each of 4,000 feed lines with one query and up to one update, so up to 8,000 requests. Below, version 0.2 in four boxes. Read: the distinct FieldLink IDs are split into chunks of 200 and each chunk is one query with an In condition, about 20 requests. Plan, a pure function in memory: every line is decided with the status rules, several lines of one work order are folded into one write with the final status, and skipped, not found and ambiguous lines are counted. Write: ExecuteMultiple batches of 100 UpdateRequest items, each with its row version, with ContinueOnError true and ReturnResponses false, about 40 requests. Second pass: only rows whose update returned a version conflict are read and planned again, once. A legend maps per-item results: no fault means applied; error 0x80040265 means refused by a plug-in; error 0x80060882 means the row version did not match and the row goes to the second pass; anything else is failed. Total about 60 requests.
svg.text: v0.1 (lesson 76): for each line → query the work order → decide → update
4,000 queries + up to 4,000 updates = up to 8,000 requests, 8,000 round trips. The request-count limit is 6,000 per 5 minutes.
Fold lines of one work order
Per-item result → how the lines of that work order are counted
No fault → Applied Fault 0x80040265 (a plug-in said no) → Refused, not retried
Fault 0x80060882 (row version does not match) → Conflicts, goes to the second pass Any other fault → Failed
Total ≈ 60 requests. The summary counts feed lines exactly as v0.1 did; intermediate statuses of folded lines are not written.
